abstract: We introduce two multiple qubit controlled-unitary gates with different working principles. We employ these gates and existing quantum gates to propose simple and efficient algorithms that generate multi-term orthonormal entangled Bell-like bases. All algorithms thus far known for constructing entangled bases turn out to be special cases of our method. The Bell-like states in any basis is superposition of $2^{m}$-terms with equal probabilities (that is, their amplitudes being $\pm 1/\sqrt{2^{m}}$). The orthogonality of the basis does not permit arbitrary amplitudes. The quantum correlations of these bases are investigated; we find that the Bell-like bases obtained using different controlled-unitaries have different entanglement contents. We also learn that monogamy score is able to distinguish these bases in the situations where other quantum correlations fail to do so indicating that monogamy score is a more fundamental quantum correlation measure. Our approach can be extended to qudit systems as well.

specification.problem: Construct, by a quantum circuit, an orthonormal basis of n-qubit 'Bell-like' entangled states in which every basis state is an equal-weight superposition of exactly 2^m computational-basis terms with amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m), generalizing the standard Bell basis (n=2, m=1).
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest useful construction chosen by the reconstruction agent (not taken from the abstract): an n-qubit basis with 2^m-term states produced by Hadamards on m control qubits followed by a classical-reversible controlled map C_f onto the remaining n-m target qubits, with the explicit tiny instance n=3, m=2, f(k)=k_1 XOR k_2. Outside scope: the paper's two specific multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates and their 'working principles', the proof that all previously known entangled-basis constructions are special cases, the entanglement/quantum-correlation comparison, the monogamy-score analysis, and the qudit extension.

equations.label: Bell-like state form
equations.description: Every basis state is an equal-probability superposition of exactly 2^m distinct computational-basis terms with real amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m).
equations.abstract_quote: The Bell-like states in any basis is superposition of $2^{m}$-terms with equal probabilities (that is, their amplitudes being $\pm 1/\sqrt{2^{m}}$)
equations.justification: Direct transcription of the amplitude/term-count statement in the abstract.
assumptions: Terms t_j are distinct computational-basis states so that the squared amplitudes sum to 1.

equations.label: Orthonormality of the basis
equations.description: The 2^n Bell-like states form an orthonormal basis of the n-qubit Hilbert space.
equations.abstract_quote: generate multi-term orthonormal entangled Bell-like bases
equations.justification: Inferred from the word 'orthonormal bases'; a basis of n qubits must contain 2^n mutually orthogonal unit vectors. Labelling by (a,b) is the agent's choice.
assumptions: Labelling of basis states by the computational-basis input (a,b) of the generating circuit.

equations.label: Hadamard layer on the control register
equations.description: m Hadamards create the 2^m-term equal-weight superposition with ±1 signs fixed by the input label a.
equations.justification: Standard identity for the m-fold tensor power of the Hadamard gate.

equations.label: Controlled-XOR gate and generating unitary (chosen construction)
equations.latex: C_f\,|k\rangle|b\rangle = |k\rangle\,|b\oplus f(k)\rangle,\qquad U = C_f\,\bigl(H^{\otimes m}\otimes I^{\otimes (n-m)}\bigr)
equations.description: A multi-qubit controlled gate that XORs a Boolean function of the control string into the target register; composed with the Hadamard layer it defines the generating circuit U.
equations.justification: The abstract names 'multiple qubit controlled-unitary gates' but does not define them; C_f is a generic reversible stand-in chosen by the agent so that a concrete construction exists. It is NOT claimed to be either of the paper's two gates.
assumptions: f is an arbitrary Boolean map; for the output to be entangled f must be non-constant.
The paper's gates may act differently (e.g., non-permutation unitaries); this choice is a placeholder.

equations.label: Generated Bell-like basis state
equations.description: Output of the chosen circuit on computational input (a,b). Since U is unitary and inputs are orthonormal, the 2^n outputs are orthonormal (eq_2); each has exactly 2^m distinct terms (distinct k) with amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m), matching eq_1.
equations.justification: Follows exactly (no approximation) from eq_3 and eq_4 by linearity; equality is exact.

equations.label: Tiny explicit instance n=3, m=2, f(k)=k_1 XOR k_2
equations.description: Two of the eight orthonormal 4-term states (qubit 1 leftmost = most significant; label string ab read as integer, e.g. 00,0 -> 0 and 10,1 -> 5).
equations.justification: Direct evaluation of eq_5 for the chosen instance; third qubit equals parity of first two XORed with b.
assumptions: Instance parameters chosen by the agent for minimality.

registers.name: control
registers.role: receives H^{⊗m}; its 2^m basis strings k index the terms of the Bell-like state; qubit 1 is the leftmost/most significant

registers.name: target
registers.role: receives b ⊕ f(k) via the multi-qubit controlled gate C_f; written to the right of the control register in kets

specification.initial_state: Computational basis state |a⟩|b⟩ with a ∈ {0,1}^m, b ∈ {0,1}^{n-m} (all 2^n inputs enumerate the whole basis); for the tiny instance, e.g. |000⟩.

steps.description: Prepare the control and target registers in the computational basis state |a⟩|b⟩ labelling the desired basis element.
Apply H to each of the m control qubits to create the equal-weight 2^m-term superposition with sign pattern (-1)^{a·k}.
Apply the multi-qubit controlled gate C_f (controls: control register; targets: target register), XORing f(k) into the target register.
The output is the Bell-like basis state |B_{a,b}⟩ with exactly 2^m terms and amplitudes ±1/sqrt(2^m); running over all (a,b) yields the full orthonormal basis.

specification.measurement: None is required for state generation. Optional verification: measure all n qubits in the computational basis; for a correct |B_{a,b}⟩ the 2^m strings (k, b⊕f(k)) each appear with probability 2^{-m} and no other strings appear.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Optional: estimate outcome frequencies and compare with the uniform distribution over the 2^m predicted strings; sign (phase) information is not accessible from computational-basis statistics alone.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the agent chose the single construction of eq_4 and the tiny instance n=3, m=2, f(k)=k_1⊕k_2.
Register ordering: control register (qubit 1 most significant) is written left of the target register; the label string ab is read as a big-endian integer.

The generic controlled-XOR gate C_f is a placeholder standing in for the paper's undefined controlled-unitary gates and is not claimed to reproduce their specific working principles or entanglement properties.
